title: RAW_UNSCREENED: Wetterpaare mit einer Ausnahme im Labelinventar
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: f77r exposes otedy/qotedy, otol/qotol, otaiin/qotaiin and okaiin/qokaiin as exact label/prose form pairs; a paired atmospheric inventory may contain one deliberately unmatched phenomenon, unlike a generic name register.

design.scope_description: Only already exposed f77r text/labels and cached Aristotle I.9-12 source; no new image or selector.
design.mechanism: A meteorological table pairs upper/lower phenomena and preserves one unpaired exception; rival treats all q/base pairs as ordinary names or labels.
design.unit: Exact whole-form sequences at named f77r loci.
design.contrast: Asymmetric phenomenon-pair inventory versus uniform label/name register
design.prediction: The pair model predicts a stable q/base pairing matrix with one unmatched row/column and distinct partner contexts; the uniform register predicts no privileged exception after exact label/prose direction is controlled.
concrete_observations: GDT930 lists the four exact shorter/longer form pairs and their label/prose loci; Aristotle I.11 explicitly gives rain/dew and snow/hoar-frost correspondences but no lower hail counterpart.
linked_consequences: A paired table needs one written exception and partner-specific contexts; a uniform register needs the same document function for every pair.
design.nearest_rival: Asymmetric phenomenon-pair inventory versus uniform label/name register
design.distinguishing_observation: Predeclare pair cells from exact forms and score partner-context asymmetry before assigning phenomenon names; do not select “hail” from the unmatched cell post hoc.
assumption_costs: Aristotle is an external architecture prior
design.strongest_likely_failure: The form pairs may be ordinary q-derivations or label/name reuse, and the f77r inventory may not contain the historical exception.
